name: Example Cloud managed identity (EU regions)
description: Keycloak 26.7.3 run for many tenants in two EU regions, behind a TLS-terminating ingress.
comment: DRAFT EXAMPLE. Keycloak run as a managed service, with the change core's capability facts. Each interface takes them from the product interface it realises. Values are illustrative.

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: ssl_ecdh_curve X25519MLKEM768:X25519; certificate ECDSA P-256 from the internal CA

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Groups and suites are the JVM defaults (jdk.tls.namedGroups not set). Server certificate RSA-2048 from the internal CA.

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: TLS mode set in the JDBC URL

interfaces.name: TLS to the corporate external identity provider
Mutual TLS between the two Keycloak replicas

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Product-generated RSA-2048 key, rotated every 30 days (cannot be changed by configuration).

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Not configurable beyond the JVM named groups

interfaces.name: HTTP from the ingress to Keycloak (port 8080)

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: http-enabled=true. Carries tokens and credentials in clear inside the cluster.

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: health-enabled=true. The management interface inherits the main server's scheme, which is HTTP here.

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Inherits the main listener TLS settings by default

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Realm defaultSignatureAlgorithm=ES256. Client 'legacy-portal' overrides it to RS256.

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Signature algorithm is set per realm (defaultSignatureAlgorithm) and per client

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Signature algorithm is set per client

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Accepted algorithms set per identity provider
